title: Software-Style Hardware Debugging: A Hardware Generation, Simulation and Debugging Framework
problem: Hardware verification still relies on traditional RTL workflows, creating a bottleneck in design-verification iteration efficiency and limiting the use of modern debugging techniques.
motivation: Hardware design iteration cycles are slow compared to software; bringing software debugging paradigms to hardware can significantly accelerate development.
method: ComoPy framework lets you simulate and debug hardware designs using familiar software techniques. You can set breakpoints (pausing points to inspect code) and trace execution on hardware description language source lines, then hot-reload changes (recompile and reload without restarting) for quick debug-fix cycles. The framework lets you dynamically switch between fast low-level RTL simulation (register-transfer level, the detailed gate-by-gate logic) and higher-level HDL execution (hardware description language), letting you balance speed against visibility for each debugging task.
key_novelty: The core idea is bringing software debugging techniques (breakpoints, tracing, hot-reloading) to hardware design verification by executing the hardware description language natively in a programming language.
contributions: Host language native simulation enabling breakpoints and tracing on HDL source lines
Software-style hot-reloading for incremental debug-fix iterations
Dynamic switching between RTL and HDL execution levels
limitations: Case studies limited to two examples (Sodor-clone processor and database accelerator); broader evaluation needed.
